name: Kwoma
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

tone_statements.citation: Zemp, Hugo & Christian Kaufmann. 1969. Pour une transcription automatique des « langages tambourinés » mélanésiens (Un exemple kwoma, Nouvelle-Guinée). L'Homme 9(2): 38-88. DOI 10.3406/hom.1969.367047. (Reprinted 1976 in Sebeok & Umiker-Sebeok (eds), Speech Surrogates: Drum and Whistle Systems, Approaches to Semiotics 23/2, ch. 63, DOI 10.1515/9783110804423-034.)
tone_statements.quote: La langue des Kwoma et de leurs voisins n'a pas encore été étudiée jusqu'à présent d'une façon approfondie3. Ce qui est sûr, c'est qu'il s'agit d'une langue non austronésienne (NA) qui n'est apparentée que de très loin à la famille linguistique Ndu, très répandue au Sépik4. Ce n'est pas une langue à tons. Cependant certaines influences de langue austronésienne sont à noter.
tone_statements.translation: The language of the Kwoma and their neighbours has not so far been studied in depth[3]. What is certain is that it is a non-Austronesian (NA) language, only very distantly related to the Ndu family, which is widespread in the Sepik[4]. It is not a tone language. However, certain Austronesian-language influences should be noted. (fn.3: two SIL teams work in the area, one among the Kwoma at Mariwei; fn.4: Laycock 1965, The Ndu Language Family)
tone_statements.locator: p.40 (section II 'Notes ethnographiques sur le « langage tambouriné » des Kwoma'; para. 'Les Kwoma'; digits 3 and 4 in the quote are footnote calls)

audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: The catalog codes Kwoma as fixed-dominant initial stress on the strength of a Wikipedia sentence with an empty cite/loc/grade. The primary source behind that sentence, Kooyers, Kooyers & Bee 1971 (Te Reo 14), was downloaded from the Linguistic Society of New Zealand's open archive and scanned: p. 41, section 4, states verbatim "Non-phonemic stress falls on the initial syllable of each word." This confirms the classification (fixed initial, non-contrastive) and should replace Wikipedia as the deciding citation, with locator 'p. 41, sec. 4 Distribution' and an upgraded strength of the evidence (primary phonology article by the SIL fieldworkers, 1961-66 fieldwork). Kooyers 1974 (held pp. 9-74 via Rosetta Project) and Bowden 1997 (held, ANU open access) are silent on word stress and defer to the 1971 article. sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Read online: the SPA 53 Washkuk inventory has 31 segments (24 consonants incl. prenasalised and labialised series, 7 vowels) and no tone segments, i.e. the database codes Kwoma as toneless on the basis of Kooyers, Kooyers & Bee 1971 (which itself reports only non-phonemic word-initial stress).
